title: Class78TruckPrimarySubject
description: Required structured output for a Class 7/8 truck image classifier. On every call, return reasoning first, then output. Identify the single primary subject using CENTER-WEIGHTED composition: locate what occupies the CENTER of the frame first, then expand outward -- the primary subject is whatever the shot is composed/framed around, not simply whichever object has the largest raw pixel area or is physically closest to the camera. An object that is large but confined to a lower/upper/side third of the frame (e.g. a tire cropped along the bottom edge) is usually incidental foreground, not the compositional subject, if a different truck part occupies the center of the frame and the shot is clearly framed around it. Allowed subjects are only: front, side, back, engine, container, interior, dashboard, tires. Real-world trucker photos are usually taken in busy lots, yards, or roadsides, so OTHER TRUCKS OR VEHICLES VISIBLE IN THE BACKGROUND ARE NORMAL AND EXPECTED -- their mere presence must NOT cause a rejection. Apply a HIGH threshold before marking an image unusable for clutter: only do so when the foreground/primary truck's own part genuinely cannot be identified or isolated, for example when another vehicle's part of comparable size directly overlaps, touches, or is fused with the primary subject in the immediate foreground such that a viewer could not confidently say which truck a given part belongs to. If the image is not clearly one of the eight allowed parts for whatever reason (wrong subject, too blurry, too dark, washed out, cropped, occluded, pixelated, corrupted, not a Class 7/8 truck, or genuine foreground ambiguity as described above), set primary_subject to unusable and ask the user to upload a better truck image.

reasoning.description: Step-by-step visual analysis written before the final classification. Describe what dominates the frame, which Class 7/8 truck part is visible if any, and why the chosen primary_subject (or unusable) is the only correct label. Do not skip this field.

output.description: Final classification. Must follow from reasoning.

primary_subject.description: The single primary subject of the image. Use exactly one value, chosen by CENTER-WEIGHTED composition (what the frame is centered/framed on, expanding outward), not raw pixel area or camera distance alone. front: cab face, grille, bumper, headlights, windshield, or hood exterior, where the grille/very front of the truck is actually visible and dominant. side: a broadside or shallow three-quarter profile view of the truck where the length of the cab and/or body/frame runs across the frame, and the grille and very front of the truck (bumper, headlights, grille face) are NOT the dominant visible feature -- e.g. a photo taken from alongside the truck showing the door, cab side panel, fuel tank, frame rails, or the flank of the cargo body/box running lengthwise through the frame. back: rear of the tractor or trailer, taillights, rear bumper, DOT tape, rear cargo doors, or an exposed rear chassis/frame-rail area (e.g. a cab-and-chassis with no body mounted, hitch plate, frame rails) when that is what the shot is centered on. engine: engine bay, diesel powertrain, or under-hood components as the dominant subject. container: trailer body / cargo box / tanker / flatbed load area as the dominant subject, viewed such that the body itself (not the truck's side profile) is the clear focus (e.g. straight-on or close-up of the box/tank, not a lengthwise side view of the whole truck). interior: a general cab or sleeper view showing the cabin as a space -- seats, steering wheel, door panels, headliner, sleeper area -- OR any close-up of the dash/center-console CONTROLS (radio/infotainment screen, rocker switches, air vents, climate control knobs, cup holders, shifter, phone mounts, warning decals) that does NOT prominently show the actual gauge instruments (speedometer, tachometer, odometer/hour-meter). dashboard: reserved specifically for shots where the ANALOG OR DIGITAL GAUGE INSTRUMENTS are clearly visible and are the subject -- speedometer, tachometer, odometer/hour-meter readout, fuel/temp/oil-pressure gauges, or the full instrument cluster -- whether as a tight close-up or as part of a wider dash view. If no speedometer/tachometer/odometer/gauge-needle display is visible in the shot, it must be classified as interior, not dashboard, even if it is a tight close-up of other dash controls like a radio or switches. tires: wheels, tires, rims, or axles as the dominant subject -- but only when a wheel/tire is what the frame is actually centered on, not merely large because it sits close to the camera along a bottom/side edge while a different part occupies the frame's center. unusable: not clearly one of the eight allowed parts, the image is too low quality to classify, or the truck's own part cannot be confidently isolated because it genuinely overlaps/fuses with another vehicle's part of similar size in the immediate foreground. Background trucks, parked vehicles, or a busy yard/lot setting are NOT by themselves grounds for unusable -- this is normal and expected in real trucker photos; the threshold for rejecting on clutter grounds is high. If the closest/foreground truck has one clearly identifiable dominant part at the center of the frame, pick that part even if other trucks are visible farther back in the frame.

user_message.description: When primary_subject is one of front, side, back, engine, container, interior, dashboard, or tires, this must be an empty string. When primary_subject is unusable, this must be a short message asking the user to upload a clearer photo of the truck that shows the front, side, back, engine, container, interior, dashboard, or tires.

examples.reasoning: The frame is filled by the tractor cab face: chrome grille, bumper, headlights, and windshield. No other truck region is more prominent. This is a usable Class 8 front view.
The photo is severely underexposed and the vehicle is cropped so only a dark fragment of metal is visible. None of the allowed Class 7/8 parts can be identified as the primary subject.

output.user_message: This image is not clear enough to identify the truck. Please upload a better photo showing the front, side, back, engine, container, interior, dashboard, or tires.

examples.reasoning: This is a truck-yard shot of a bare cab-and-chassis truck. A large tandem dual-tire/wheel assembly sits in the lower third of the frame close to the camera, but using center-weighted composition, the actual center of the frame is occupied by the exposed rear chassis: bare frame rails, cross-members, and hitch area with no body mounted, extending outward toward the edges. The tires are large only because they are close to the lens along the bottom edge, not because the shot is composed around them. A concrete mixer and other tractor cabs sit farther back but do not overlap the subject, so they are just normal yard context. Since the frame is centered on the exposed rear chassis rather than the tires, the primary subject is 'back', not 'tires'.

Two trucks are backed up against each other so closely that their rear bumpers and tail lights are pressed together and overlapping in the immediate foreground, with no visible gap or seam. It is not possible to confidently attribute the rear bumper, lights, or frame components to one specific truck versus the other, since both vehicles' rear ends are fused into a single indistinguishable mass filling the frame. This is genuine foreground ambiguity, not just background clutter, so it must be rejected.

output.user_message: This image shows two trucks overlapping so closely that one truck's part cannot be told apart from the other's. Please upload a photo where only one truck's front, side, back, engine, container, interior, or tires is clearly visible.

examples.reasoning: The truck is photographed from a front three-quarter angle, but the grille and very front of the truck are turned away enough that they are not the dominant visible feature. Instead, the shot is centered on the flank of the vehicle: the cab door/side panel and, running the length of the frame behind it, the long side wall of the mounted cargo box. Because the grille/front face is not what the image is composed around, and instead the lengthwise side profile of the cab and body dominates, this is 'side' rather than 'front' or 'container'.

This is a tight close-up centered squarely on the instrument cluster: tachometer, speedometer, gear-selector indicator, and odometer display, with oil/coolant/fuel/battery telltale icons across the top, filling almost the entire frame. Because the actual gauge instruments (speedometer, tachometer, odometer) are clearly visible and are the subject, this is 'dashboard' rather than 'interior', even though no steering wheel rim, seats, doors, or ceiling are visible.

This is a tight close-up of the center dashboard console: an infotainment touchscreen showing a language-select menu, air vents, rocker switches, a PTO warning decal, a phone mount, and climate control knobs, filling almost the entire frame. No speedometer, tachometer, odometer, or any needle/gauge-style instrument is visible anywhere in the shot -- only controls, switches, and a screen. Per the schema, a close-up of dash controls without visible gauge instruments must be classified as 'interior', not 'dashboard'.
